bibl.author: P. Ovidius Naso
bibl.title: P. Ovidii Nasonis operum tomus primus
bibl.ref: Washington and Lee University Special Collections, PA6519 .A2 1751, volume 1
bibl.note: One-based viewer images 175–176; printed page numbers are 44 lower. Archive page labels differ from both. The actual images, rather than another witness or uncorrected OCR, supply the readings.

normalization.p: Source spelling, capitalization, punctuation, written ampersands and visible accents are retained. Long s and typographic ligatures are represented by standard s and constituent letters. Letter spacing in display capitals and quotation glyph shapes may be represented schematically. No modern-edition readings are substituted.

segmentation.p: Each l represents one canonical verse, with stable numbering and a link to its existing image region. Source verse order and headings are retained. Couplet grouping and canonical line numbers are editorial. A displaced word may remain within its verse with its position marked.

Compared actual line starts on each full-page image, including at page transitions. This setting uses a recurring couplet inset; the explicit list records the observed inset starts in this poem, not a rule inferred from verse-number parity. Initial capitals and drop capitals vary the apparent left edge.

correction.p: Uncertain readings remain locally marked with unclear or gap. Observations and uncertainties are documented for a different source reader; ink colour alone does not establish erasure or a separate hand.

revisionDesc.change: First reader inspected and transcribed all 48 verses from the source images; independent source review pending.

Independent reviewer inspected every extant verse in full-page context and enlarged source-image bands, corrected source readings and page furniture, and checked observed line starts. Review report and exact XML/report hashes are recorded in the companion ledger.

Fresh corpus source reading rechecked all 48 verses, every evidence note, headings, page furniture and full-page line starts. No further verse wording changes were supported. Prior independent second-pass history is retained; changed readings were additionally corroborated from native crops by /root/w_review_c. See W-3.3-second-pass.md.

lg.label: Elegia III. De amica, quae pejeraverat.
lg.l: ESse Deos, i, crede. fidem jurata fefellit:
Et facies illi, quae fuit ante, manet.
Quam longos habuit nondum jurata capillos,
Tam longos, postquam numina lusit, habet.
Candida candorem roseo suffusa rubore
Ante stetit: niveo lucet in ore rubor,
Pes erat exiguus: pedis est aptissima forma.
Longa decensque fuit: longa decensque manet.
Argutos habuit, radiant ut sidus, ocellos;
Per quos mentita est perfida saepe mihi.
Scilicet aeterno falsum jurare puellis
Dî quoque concedunt; formaque numen habet.
Perque suos illam nuper jurasse recordor,
Perque meos oculos; & doluere mei.
Dicite, Dî; si vos impune fefellerit illa,
Alterius meritis cur ego damna tuli?
At non invidiae vobis Cepheïa virgo est,
Pro male formosâ jussa parente mori.
Non satis est, quod vos habui sine pondere testes,
Et mecum lusos ridet inulta Deos:
Ut sua per nostram redimat perjuria poenam,
Victima deceptus decipientis ero?
Aut sine re nomen Deus est, frustraque timetur;
Et stultâ populos credulitate movet:
Aut, si quis Deus est, teneras amat ille puellas;
Et nimium solas omnia posse jubet.
Nobis fatifero Mavors adcingitur ense:
Nos petit invictâ Palladis hasta manu.
Nobis flexibiles curvantur Apollinis arcus:
In nos alta Jovis dextera fulmen habet.
Formosas Superi metuunt offendere laesi:
Atque ultro, quae se non timuere, timent.
Et quisquam pia tura focis imponere curet?
Certe plus animi debet inesse viris.
Juppiter igne suo lucos jaculatur & arces.
Missaque perjuras tela ferire vetat.
Tot meruere peti. Semele miserabilis arsit:
Officio est illi poena reperta suo.
At si venturo se subduxisset amanti,
Non pater in Baccho matris haberet onus.
Quid queror, & toti facio convicia coelo?
Dî quoque habent oculos: Dî quoque pectus habent.
Si Deus ipse forem; numen sine fraude liceret
Femina mendaci falleret ore meum.
Ipse ego jurarem verum jurare puellas;
Et non de tetricis dicerer esse Deus.
Tu tamen illorum moderatius utere dono:
Aut oculis certè parce, puella, meis.
